observation_summary: The compiler fails to resolve type aliases in JSDoc annotations when they appear before the alias definition, resulting in 'Unknown type' errors.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the compiler's type resolution logic during the traversal of the AST. The compiler is unable to correctly map the alias (e.g., 'Foo.Bar') to its fully qualified name ('foo.Foo.Bar') when the annotation is processed before the alias is defined. This is a procedural logic error in how the compiler handles scope and type resolution during the traversal of the code, which is best classified as an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: bug_report_description: 'Type aliases cannot be used in type annotations before their definitions'
stack_trace_excerpt: 'ERROR - Bad type annotation. Unknown type Foo.Bar'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves the relationship between the alias and its definition, the root cause is the procedural logic (algorithm) used by the compiler to resolve these types during traversal.
This is not a missing capability or design-level omission, but rather an incorrect implementation of the existing type resolution algorithm.
